answer: A sock-puppet farm must pay that stake per fake identity plus repeated beacon compute, and since attestations only count from already-staked peers, costs compound faster than any parallel identity can recoup. Each agent must burn a proof-of-work beacon tied to its node kernel before joining, and every epoch it stakes a small ocean of tokens that decays unless peers attest real task throughput. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
